concerns.text: Task T014b-NEW (Classifier Proxy) is marked as [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depends on T014 (Classifier Runner). The description states 'Depends on: T014', yet the [P] tag implies it can run independently. This violates the 'Producer before consumer' rule and creates a false parallel opportunity.

Task T014b-DOC depends on T014b-NEW, but T014b-NEW is marked [P]. If T014b-NEW is truly parallel-safe, T014b-DOC should not depend on it sequentially unless T014b-NEW is a prerequisite artifact. The [P] tag on T014b-NEW contradicts the sequential dependency chain required for the documentation task.

Task T022 (Matching) depends on T017b (Semantic Similarity), but T017b is marked as 'Critical Path, not [P]'. However, T022 itself is not marked [P] despite being in a phase where parallel execution is encouraged. The dependency chain T017b -> T022 is correct, but the lack of explicit sequential markers in the 'Dependencies & Execution Order' section for T022 vs T017b is ambiguous.

Task T033a (Cohort Analysis) depends on T014b-NEW and T014. T014b-NEW is marked [P], but T033a is not. The dependency is valid, but the [P] tag on the producer (T014b-NEW) without a corresponding sequential marker on the consumer (T033a) in the 'Parallel Opportunities' section creates confusion about when T033a can actually start.

Task T017b (Semantic Similarity) is described as 'Critical Path, not [P]', but the task list does not explicitly state which tasks depend on it in the 'Within Each User Story' section, only in the 'Critical Cross-Phase Dependencies' section. This separation makes the dependency flow harder to trace semantically.
